doc.title: Peter Vacher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001

title: What drew him to Armstrong, Oliver and Jelly Roll
summary: He loved the energy, rhythmic drive and emotion of the black innovators, informed by autobiographies he read.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Put it in words for me if you can, what made them so distinguishable?

The energy, which is still a powerful factor to me; the rhythmic drive; and just that sense that something was kind of bursting out of the grooves that was quite unlike anything else. To me then, Beiderbecke and Trumbauer seemed effete. All right? A little restrained. I like that sense of, you know, all out emotion. I think it was the emotion in other words. And I suppose by then I’d started to read a lot, you know I’d read Louis’ autobiography by then. I’d read Bechet’s autobiography. I’d read, Rudi Blesh’s Shining Trumpets. There was a whole literature that was kind of inspiring and informing at the same time. And I think the focus then, and probably has continued to be, it was on the great black innovators. That sense that the momentum of the music came from these key people, from Jelly Roll, from Louis, from King Oliver if you like. They were the play makers. So I think that’s what hit me hardest.
